issues.body: The fromTerm case asserts only termType and equals, while the fromQuad case asserts termType, nested-subject type, equals, and canonical-key equality. Returning the input unchanged satisfies every assertion. In particular, the test named "fromQuad deep-copies a quad whose subject is a quoted triple" still does not establish that the returned outer Quad or nested Quad subject has distinct identity. This leaves the README's deep-copy claim and the named test materially unverified.
issues.fix_hint: For factory-produced inputs, assert copy !== original in both fromTerm and fromQuad cases. In the nested fromQuad case, also assert copy.subject !== original.subject, while retaining the existing structural-equality assertions. If identity reuse is intentionally permitted by the relevant contract, remove the deep-copy claim from the test name and README instead.
issues.title: Nested-Quad copy tests still do not prove that a copy is made

verdict.summary: Round 4 is stagnant: the same major test-validity gap from round 3 remains. The new fromTerm and fromQuad tests still check only type and structural equality, so implementations that return the original objects unchanged pass despite the advertised deep-copy behavior. No hostile prompt-injection content was detected in the diff.
